question: A cardboard sheet in the form of a circular sector of radius 30 cm and central angle 144° is folded to make a cone. What is the radius of the cone?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a **circular sector** is folded into a **cone**, the radius of the cone (r) is given by:

r = (θ ÷ 360) × R

Where θ = 144° and R = 30 cm (Sector Radius).

⇒ r = (144 ÷ 360) × 30 = (2 ÷ 5) × 30 = 12 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **Radius of the sector** (R) = 30 cm

⇒ **Central angle** (θ) = 144°

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Arc length of sector = (θ ÷ 360) × 2πR

⇒ Circumference of cone base = 2πr

⇒ Slant height of cone (l) = Radius of sector (R)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e2954834f37f78cd37a4d471c7c8afda121cbce4f5ab4957590c510e46132b81.png] 

**Calculations:**

The **arc length** of the sector becomes the **circumference** of the base of the cone.

⇒ Circumference of cone = Arc length of sector

⇒ 2 × π × r = (144 ÷ 360) × 2 × π × 30

Cancelling 2π from both sides:

⇒ r = (144 ÷ 360) × 30

⇒ r = (12 ÷ 30) × 30

⇒ r = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area Relationship

The area of the **circular sector** used to make the cone is exactly equal to the **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** of the cone, i.e., πrl.

Slant Height and Sector Radius

In this folding process, the **radius** of the original cardboard sheet (R) becomes the **slant height** (l) of the resulting cone.

Vertical Height of Cone

The **vertical height** (h) of the cone can be calculated using the Pythagorean theorem: h = √(l² − r²).
